bad.why: It is about someone above or ahead of you who blocks your way, not any nuisance. Say meiwaku da or urusai.

mean: to witness something with one's own eyes
lit: to have it in the space right before one's eyes; ma is an old reading of the character for eye, as in mabuta (eyelid)

use.how: Takes を: 被害の大きさを目の当たりにした. Said of seeing in person something striking or significant: a disaster, a reality, a great performance.

near.diff: 目を疑う is not believing what one sees; 目の当たりにする simply says one saw it oneself, directly and up close.

cue: You had read about the flood damage, but standing in the ruined town yourself, you finally grasp how bad it really was.

ctx.s: 初[はじ]めて本物[ほんもの]のオーロラを{目[ま]の当[あ]たりにした}。
ctx.en: For the first time I saw a real aurora with my own eyes.

ctx.s: 「話[はなし]には聞[き]いていたけど、実際[じっさい]に{目[ま]の当[あ]たりにする}と驚[おどろ]くね。」
ctx.en: "I'd heard about it, but seeing it for real is still a shock, isn't it."

ctx.s: 被災地[ひさいち]を訪[おとず]れ、地震[じしん]の被害[ひがい]の大[おお]きさを{目[ま]の当[あ]たりにした}。
ctx.en: Visiting the disaster area, I saw for myself how great the earthquake damage was.

ctx.s: プロの演奏[えんそう]を{目[ま]の当[あ]たりにして}、自分[じぶん]との差[さ]を思[おも]い知[し]った。
ctx.en: Seeing a professional perform right in front of me, I realised how far I had to go.

ctx.s: 祖母[そぼ]は、戦後[せんご]の町[まち]が大[おお]きく変[か]わっていくのを{目[ま]の当[あ]たりにして}きた。
ctx.en: My grandmother has seen with her own eyes how the town changed after the war.

ctx.s: 研修[けんしゅう]で医療[いりょう]の現場[げんば]の厳[きび]しさを{目[ま]の当[あ]たりにし}、医者[いしゃ]になる決意[けつい]が固[かた]まった。
ctx.en: Seeing the harsh reality of hospital work during training made my resolve to become a doctor firm.

bad.s: 昨日[きのう]、駅前[えきまえ]で友達[ともだち]を{目[ま]の当[あ]たりにした}。
bad.en: (meant: I saw a friend in front of the station yesterday)
bad.why: It is for witnessing something striking or significant. Just spotting a person is mikaketa.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]の苦労話[くろうばなし]を電話[でんわ]で{目[ま]の当[あ]たりにした}。
bad.en: (meant: I heard about his hardships first-hand on the phone)
bad.why: It means seeing directly before one's eyes. Hearing something on the phone is not witnessing it.
